subject: FalconSight — ops readout: latency & throughput requirements + next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@falconsight.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: FalconSight — ops readout: latency & throughput requirements + next steps

Thanks for the time today, Samir — great conversation. Below is a concise readout from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Summary of pain / goals
- Primary pain: production instability and cost spikes when serving embeddings and short-chat flows (search + assist).
- Primary goal: predictable 95th- and 99th-percentile latency for user-facing flows while reducing per-request cost 20–30%.
- Secondary: full auditability for query provenance and integration with GCP IAM/KMS.

Key technical constraints you mentioned
- Average request: 64 tokens (prompt + response); peak request size occasionally 512 tokens for batch summarization jobs.
- Target steady-state throughput: ~1,000 requests/minute for assistant flows, with 5–10 minute bursts to 3,000 rpm during promotions.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 200ms for single-turn assistant responses (up to 128 tokens); p99 <= 500ms.
- Model family: you plan to evaluate 7B/13B variants for assistant, 70B for selective summarization. On-prem deployment for PHI-adjacent workloads later this year.
- Security: SOC2 in place for production data, but you need evidence of per-tenant audit logs and KMS integration for keys-at-rest.

Possible Redwood fit & ops considerations
- Hosted + Dedicated hybrid: host low-risk assistant traffic on Redwood Hosted for quick ramp; Dedicated pools for high-throughput bursts and sensitive workloads.
- Caching & KV prefix reuse could reduce token work for repeated prompts (good fit for your search-assist patterns).
- Quantized model variants for summarization to hit burst capacity without 2x cost.

Proposed next steps (action owners / timing)
1) Deep-dive ops session (1–1.5h) to map traffic profiles and confirm model variants to benchmark — week of Oct 18 — owner: Marissa (schedule).
2) Security questionnaire + evidence exchange — Samir to share initial answers; Marissa & Laura to return Redwood artifacts by Oct 20.
3) 2-week PoC run: measure p95/p99 under representative load (k6 scenario) with telemetry exported to your Datadog — target start Oct 25. Deliverable: performance report + cost projections.
4) Procurement / licensing discussion after PoC — timeline: Nov.

Attachments: falconsight-infra-sketch-v1.png (infra sketch you shared in call) — included for reference. Also attached a lightweight PoC runbook template (redwood-poc-runbook.xlsx).

Questions outstanding for Samir
- Which GPU SKUs are available in your environment today (A100/H100)?
- Any surge protection (API gateway) in front of model inference?
- Is there an internal SLA or customer-facing latency requirement we should map to?

Thanks — I’ll send a calendar invite for the deep-dive once I hear availability.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FalconSight — ops readout: latency & throughput requirements + next steps

Thanks Marissa — solid notes, appreciate the clarity. A few clarifications and answers below.

Clarifications from our side
- GPUs: our cloud footprint today is primarily H100s (managed via our GCP tenancy); we can run A100s but prefer H100 for the large-parameter evaluation.
- Surge protection: we front inference with an API gateway (Cloud Armor + GCLB). Most spikes are at the gateway, not model workers.
- Internal SLA: product requires p95 <= 250ms for assistant responses; customer SLAs can be negotiated depending on plan.

Model & traffic details
- Assistant: plan to start with 13B (quantized FP16) for latency-sensitive flows; hold 70B for nightly bulk summarization and selective escalations.
- Embeddings: mix of short (64 tokens) and long (512 tokens) inputs in batch pipelines; we expect embeddings to be ~40% of token volume during peak.

Security questionnaire
- Attached: falconsight-security-answers-2027-10.pdf — contains our compliance checklist and a list of required audit artifacts. We will need a KMS integration worksheet and explanation of how Redwood persists KV cache.

Timeline & PoC
- PoC sounds good. Targeting Oct 25 start is workable if we lock test scenarios this week. We will aim to provide a small representative dataset and sample traffic profile by Oct 18.

Open asks for Redwood
1) Can Redwood surface per-tenant audit logs and an export format?
2) Does the PoC support a mixed-variant routing policy (13B for low-latency, 70B fallback for heavy ops)?
3) What telemetry hooks do you provide for token-level cost attribution?

—
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, FalconSight
samir@falconsight.ai

Subject: Re: FalconSight — ops readout: latency & throughput requirements + next steps

Samir — thanks for the quick turnaround and the security doc. Short runbook/ops notes from our side below so the PoC is scoped tightly.

PoC scope (2 weeks)
- Objectives: validate p95/p99 for assistant flows at 1,000 rpm with burst to 3,000 rpm; measure per-request cost for 13B quantized vs 70B quantized; validate Datadog telemetry and audit-log exports.
- Test bed: Redwood Dedicated pool (H100-backed) + small on-hosted fallback.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-requests, and cache hit rate.
- Data residency: all test data will be treated as non-PHI; for later PHI tests we will run Private deployment model.

Runbook highlights:
- Load profile: we’ll mimic your production mixes — provide k6 scripts for assistant and embeddings.
- Mixed-variant routing: Redwood routing policy will prefer 13B for latency-sensitive calls and route to 70B when prompt length or policy triggers consolidation. We’ll validate policy in week 1 of PoC.
- Audit logs & telemetry: we can export per-request traces and token attribution to a secure S3 bucket or push to your Datadog — we’ll include a sample export by Oct 27.

Operational asks from FalconSight
- Confirm preferred PoC start date (Oct 25) and a primary contact for telemetry ingestion.
- Confirm if PHI workload will be excluded from PoC.

I’ll attach a first-draft PoC checklist in the shared Drive — link below. If there are no objections I’ll calendar the kickoff and loop infra for network/security prep.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-falconsight-poc

Best,
Laura Bennett
